Fictional life · authored game rules

Your life, so far

Game values · not predictions
Rules, sources & what this prototype leaves out

This is an authored game study, dated 23 October 2026. Points, money, health changes and event odds are game tuning, not measured Thai statistics or individual predictions. Cash changes are simplified five-year additions and costs, not wages. Graphs connect five-year snapshots.

IQ and EQ name fictional reasoning and connection attributes here. They are not psychometric test scores. The ten-point constraint is a game mechanic; strength and intelligence are not biological opposites. Starting attributes stay fixed; five-year priorities change how you spend effort.

Smoking has a modeled health and money cost, without a guaranteed happiness reward. Social drinking has a cost and a context-dependent social effect. Religion has no universal health or morality bonus. Relationship beliefs are personal values, not scores. Adult habit controls begin at 20; relationship questions appear after 15.

The scene is metaphorical: nearby buildings represent parts of a life, not a real town map. The course view shows age stations and recorded changes in priorities. It does not reveal a known death date. Mortality rolls are fictional and fixed by scenario so replays share external events; health can change the outcome.

Health assumptions require research before a calibrated release. References: WHO: HIV and AIDS. Disease-specific events, substances, historic Thai crises, treatment coverage and investment markets remain unimplemented.
